pins.desc: Iron oxide earth: one of the oldest pigments, found in cave paintings. Natural (PY43) or synthetic (PY42). Gentle and weak, it softens any colour and is great for skin tones and landscapes. On the colour mixing page of pigeonpolly.com you can see all 16 pigments: transparency, strength, staining, granulation, lightfastness and a short story for each.

pins.title: Phthalo green (PG7): Properties, History and How to Mix With It
pins.desc: Phthalocyanine green: a cool blue-green, very strong and staining. Almost never used straight: mixed with yellows, ochre or reds it gives natural greens for leaves and grass. pins.title: Black (PBk9 / PBk11): Properties, History and How to Mix With It
pins.desc: Ivory black (PBk9) is made from charred bones and is slightly warm; mars black (PBk11) is iron oxide, denser and more opaque. Black quickly makes colours dull, so use it rarely and in tiny amounts. On the colour mixing page of pigeonpolly.com you can see all 16 pigments: transparency, strength, staining, granulation, lightfastness and a short story for each.
